about.title: Pleasant Hill Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Pleasant Hill's mix of retail centers, office parks, and industrial spaces near Contra Costa Boulevard and I-680 means workplace injuries here range from warehouse falls to delivery-driver collisions. In California, workers' compensation is typically your only path against your employer, no matter who caused the accident. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your comp benefits. Navigating both systems at once can be confusing while you're also trying to recover physically. We handle workplace injury claims on a contingency basis, meaning there's no upfront cost. Our team can help you understand whether a third-party claim applies to your Pleasant Hill workplace injury.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or loading docks
Delivery or fleet vehicle collisions on the job
Injuries from defective tools or machinery
Chemical exposure or burns in warehouse settings

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California generally limits your recovery against an employer to workers' comp, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can open the door to additional compensation.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You typically have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own 2-year filing deadline, so waiting can cost you options.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an injury, and we can help you understand those protections if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse job near Contra Costa Boulevard. Do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' comp is your primary path against your employer regardless of fault. If a third party, like a delivery contractor or equipment supplier, contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate claim worth exploring. We can help sort out which applies to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' comp rights. Missing that window can complicate your claim, so it's worth reporting as soon as possible even if the injury seems minor at first.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a job injury?
items.answer: No, California law makes it illegal for employers to retaliate against workers for reporting an on-the-job injury. If you're facing pressure or discipline after reporting, we can help you understand your options and protect your rights.
